items.title: 66086_Zilner T. Randolph oral history interview
items.q: I studied there with Eddie for about four years. I took harmony, theory of harmony then... I always looked forward to coming to Eddie, because Eddie always would sit after a lesson and he would talk me all night about staying out of pool rooms.

ctx.x: Yes. So, well, I studied there with

Eddie for about four years. I took harmony, theory of harmony then, Goodrich Analysis of Music -- now, there's where you learn something about music. Then -- and I passed -- I used that with my pupils too. A lot of the information I got out of the books with Eddie Hudson, such things like -- now, you know, we use bars out of context when we say bars. There's a bar line and there's a perpendicular line, see. See, (unintelligible) line runs horizontal and this perpendicular line is the bar line.

Now, that bar line divides the staff in two measures. They rewrite the notes in the measure and if some singer or dancer or even some orchestra leader comes up and they want you to play the last two measures, they'll tell you to play the last two bars. Well, the last two bars maybe sometime on a number is the last two double bars -- the last two bars which isn't anything, and I showed them that, about the last two bars. And such things like, pick up the time. You can't pick --
